_note: Two fictional persons in the audit of T0, "Some steps in the procedure need a person." Their stances are stipulated, not anyone's judgement. They write independently: neither cites the other. E shows the nescio and the decide; F shows an interpreter who says which reading E goes by, which E does not confirm. The letters E and F are new: A-D are personas of earlier trials, and the agent's run g1 was set up for A, the real author, before the trial was turned to personas.

E (fictional author).body: Fictional person E, the author of T0 (stipulated stance). By "Some" E means the steps named in the sentences that follow: holder and settle. E knows this reading and holds it.

Fictional person E. Asked whether these steps need a person because only a person can perform them (P2) or because someone must answer for them afterwards (P4), E cannot say. Both were in mind when the sentence was written, and nothing in the draft tells them apart. E sees both readings clearly and still does not know which was meant.

Fictional person E. Whether "a person" is the particular person the step concerns (R2) or any named signer (R3), E cannot say. For a holder entry the two coincide; for a settle they come apart. E leaves this open.

Fictional person E decides to mean P4 from now on. Under P2 the sentence is a thesis about what the acts are, which the paper does not argue; under P4 it says what the record keeps, a name that answers for the step. This is a choice made now, not a report of what was meant when the sentence was written.

F (fictional reviewer).body: Fictional person F, a reviewer of the draft (stipulated stance). F reads the sentence after "Who decided?" as saying that only a person can perform these acts at all, and takes that to be the reading the author goes by. F has not asked the author.
